↳ Posted by slainte on January 26th, 2006.

No comments?

A really nice, classic Sliabh Luachra jig. Denis Murphy plays |G3 AGA|Bde gdB| and Caoimhin o’Raghallaigh and Breanndan Begley played it |G2G AGA|dgf gdB| in concert at Boston College; the setting presented, with the long B, is from Paddy Cronin’s playing (he played it crosstuned, up a set). Also good an octave low.

--DtM

↳ Posted by Dan the Man on February 3rd, 2008.

↳ Posted by The Archivist on November 12th, 2009.

Additional titles

Also known in older sources as ‘The Happy Mistake’. Similar tunes appear in O‘Neill as ’The Best in the Bag‘ and ’Miss Monroe’s‘. Appears in Bulmer and Sharpley as ’The King’s Jig‘, AKA ’The King of Jigs’, or (in Irish) Rí na bPort.

↳ Posted by rwwt on May 11th, 2011.

Re: The Munster

Appears on the album “Two Miles to Tulla” as Jackson’s Bottle of Claret, which they (in the liner notes) attribute to the 18th century piper Walter Jackson from Ballingarry, Co. Limerick, and say was published in Capt. Francis O’Neill’s Waifs and Strays of Gaelic Melody in 1922.
